beats.shot: Delivery tab, HTTP selected. Cursor opens Auth type and picks 'OAuth2 — fetch token first'; the token fields reveal. The endpoint URL is typed.
beats.vo: Some supplier A P Is won't take a static key — they want you to trade a client id and secret for a short-lived access token first. On the H T T P delivery channel, point ProcuLink at their endpoint, and pick O Auth 2 — fetch token first — as the auth type. The token fields appear.

beats.shot: Cursor fills Token URL, then Client ID, then Client secret (sample values).
beats.vo: Token U R L is where the supplier mints the token. Client id and client secret are the credentials they issued you — the secret is encrypted at rest and never shown back.

beats.shot: Cursor fills Scope (orders.write), opens the Advanced disclosure, rests on Grant type (client_credentials default).
beats.vo: Scope is the space-separated permission list the token should carry — optional if their docs don't require one. And the grant type for machine-to-machine delivery is almost always client credentials, which is the default.

beats.shot: In Advanced: Client auth toggled (request body ↔ basic header), Request format toggled (form ↔ JSON), then rest on Token response field (access_token).
beats.vo: Two advanced fields decide the wire format. Client auth sends your credentials either in the request body or as a basic header. Request format encodes that request as form data or J S O N — their docs say which. And token response field names the property holding the token; the standard is access underscore token.

beats.shot: Cursor sweeps up to the endpoint URL field, then rests on the on-screen flow note: token fetched fresh before each delivery, sent as Authorization: Bearer, never stored.
beats.vo: Here's the flow, exactly as it runs. Before each delivery, ProcuLink calls the token U R L, reads the token out of the response, and sends it as a bearer on the order request. It's fetched fresh every time and never stored — so short expiry windows are never a problem.

beats.shot: Cursor rests on the footer Test-fire button (dimmed until saved; never clicked — no mock backend).
beats.vo: Save, then test — and read a green result precisely. It means the token endpoint answered, and the supplier's endpoint answered. It still does not mean the supplier accepted an order — that can be rejected later, which is why ProcuLink tracks delivery and acceptance separately.
